meta.name: Mini-Tetra multi-Forge cluster study
meta.price_basis: USD street/retail estimates, Nov 2026, qty 1, tax/shipping excluded; assume +/-15% and re-run with --gpu-price-shock to test the ranking

winners.label: Best overall
winners.rationale: Highest weighted score: the most aggregate 16 GB+ throughput and VRAM that fits the budget, circuit and compatibility limits.
winners.head: Minisforum MS-01 (i9-13900H, 32 GB, 2 TB, 2x10G SFP+)
winners.platform: Dual-GPU mATX cube (Ryzen 5, 32 GB, 2 TB, 1000 W ATX)
winners.storage: 4 TB NVMe model cache in head, exported over NFS/SMB
stability_notes: head has 10G + 3x M.2: queue, NFS and cache do not fight for I/O
two GPUs share one PSU per chassis
large fault domain: one node failure removes 2/4 of the GPUs
UPS: prevents checkpoint/queue corruption on brownouts

head_analysis.verdict: Yes, but differentiate it by role, not by GPU. At an equal GPU count a dedicated non-GPU head costs about $983 more and adds about 2.3 stability points; it wins on score at every fleet size tested because a head that also renders shares its CPU, RAM and driver stack with the queue. A GPU in the head looks cheaper per GPU, but it puts the scheduler inside a GPU failure domain; it is worth it only if you want an interactive seat on the same box.
